summary.intent: Execute all 9 plans of Phase 71 (Share-Invite Security & IPNS Data-Integrity API) using wave-based parallel subagent execution, then run the full autonomous post-execute-phase ship loop (verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E gate → CodeRabbit → ship → resolve PR reviews → extract learnings).
summary.outcome: All 9 plans across 4 waves executed, merged, and verified (16/16 truths, 0 gaps); phase marked complete. Ship loop started: verification confirmed passed, security/validation audits spawned in parallel, and a simplify pass identified a 7-line ownership-gate duplication captured as a deferred todo rather than refactored pre-ship; transcript ends mid-ship-loop before SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit, and PR steps.

repo: This is a pnpm monorepo (apps/api, packages/sdk-core, packages/sdk, apps/web, tests/sdk-e2e, Rust crates) — generic gates defaulting to `npm test`/`npm run build` are wrong here.

`pnpm typecheck` (root script) is the true cross-plan integration check but excludes `apps/api tsc --noEmit` — errors only visible via `apps/api tsc --noEmit` are non-CI-gated and can be pre-existing noise.
Worktrees fork from live HEAD (`baseref-head`), so parallel worktree isolation is retained across waves without degrade.
sdk-e2e auth: vitest does not auto-load `.env`; `SDK_E2E_SECRET` must be explicitly aligned with the API's `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET` or requests 401 and cascade-skip downstream tests in the suite.
Worktrees created by executor agents don't get gitignored `.env` files via `pnpm install` — must be copied in manually before running e2e suites from a worktree.
D-04's `claim_count` CHECK constraint (SQLSTATE 23514) can only be truly verified live against Postgres inside a BEGIN…ROLLBACK transaction; Jest mocks the DataSource so unit tests can't prove it.
The commit-tracking helper (used after wave merges) can report `commit_failed` as a false negative even when the commit lands — always verify via `git log`.
codebase-drift gate flags 143 pre-existing structural elements as advisory noise when `last_mapped_commit: null` (repo never `/gsd-map-codebase`'d) — not a real regression signal.

Phase 71 commits already used conventional scoped subjects (`feat(71-08):`), so the ship-phase's assumed `feat 71-03:`-style reword step was likely unnecessary — must verify at that step rather than assume it's needed.
Root `SECURITY.md` is tracked in this repo; the security auditor has a known quirk of overwriting it instead of writing the phase-scoped `<phase>-SECURITY.md`.

code.finding: createInvite ownership gate (D-01/SC#1): queries ipns_records for (shareRootIpnsName, sharerId) before persisting, throws ForbiddenException on miss — duplicated in shares.service.ts createShare, flagged as extractable but deferred as a post-ship todo.

createShare duplicates the same 7-line root-ownership gate logic as share-invite.service.ts createInvite; candidate for an assertRootOwnership helper, deferred via todo rather than refactored pre-ship.
D-05/D-06: same-seq CID equivocation guard (metadataCid !== existing.latestCid → BadRequestException) and 23505→409 ConflictException translation on first-publish INSERT race, added by plan 71-04.

revokeForItems (SC#5/D-08) replaced manager.find+manager.remove with a single createQueryBuilder().delete().from(Share) scoped to sharer_id + share_root_ipns_name; revokedShares now sourced from the DELETE's affected count.

workflow: Wave-based orchestration: dispatch one subagent, confirm its worktree exists before dispatching the next in the same wave (avoids config.lock race), merge only after all wave agents return, then run a wave-scoped post-merge gate before advancing.
Post-merge gates should be scoped to what actually reached a consistent cross-plan state (e.g. skip full pnpm typecheck after Wave 1 since Wave 2 intentionally fixes TS consumers), not run blindly.

When a subagent's own check (e.g. cargo check --lib) conflicts with raw diagnostics, don't trust either in isolation — settle it by re-running the stricter check (cargo check --all-targets) against the actual merged tree.

For blocking human-verify checkpoint tasks (autonomous:false), structure the wave as sub-waves: run the autonomous plans in parallel worktrees first, then handle the checkpoint plan separately with an explicit AskUserQuestion before driving any live-stack side effects.

Before running a live-stack integration test, verify the running API process is actually serving current branch code (not a stale `node dist/main.js` build) — restart/rebuild if in doubt, since a stale server yields false failures.
For simple continuation work after a checkpoint resolves, doing it directly via git -C in the worktree is fine instead of spawning a heavier continuation agent.

friction: 71-03's Rust rename subagent reported cargo check --lib green while E0560 errors were visible in diagnostics for delete.rs/rename.rs — turned out to be stale LSP noise not present in the actual merged tree, requiring an extra verification pass.
The wave/phase tracking commit helper repeatedly false-negatived with commit_failed despite commits landing, requiring manual git log verification each time.

Live sdk-e2e run against the 71-05 checkpoint failed twice before succeeding: first due to a stale compiled API server on :3000 needing a rebuild/restart, then due to SDK_E2E_SECRET/TEST_LOGIN_SECRET mismatch causing 401 cascade-skips.
Worktree for 71-05 lacked gitignored .env files, requiring manual copy before the live-stack test could run.

AUTO_MODE (workflow.auto_advance) was true and would have silently chained into planning/discussing an entirely new, undiscussed Phase 72 — required an explicit stop-and-ask rather than auto-advancing.
